title: Marked-Poisson Limit Law for Clipped AIPW at the Critical Propensity Floor
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 graded tier subfield below the field floor: paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered results establish a feasible uniform marked-Poisson limit, fitted-law confidence intervals, random-variance limit, and law-family endpoint bridge, but only under an exact scalar quadratic boundary, uniform design, binary outcomes, a bespoke histogram learner, and fixed clipping multiplier.

They do not establish an estimator phase diagram for varying or selected clipping, robustness to unknown boundary geometry or tail exponent, or a broadly reusable nuisance-learning theorem; the framing correctly avoids claiming those extensions.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived and reviewed the learned-nuisance critical limit, fitted-law intervals, random-variance law, and fixed-law stable-to-Gaussian bridge; the math and rubric panels passed without open findings. The field-tier claim failed the general panel's breadth and paper-score gate, with achieved tier subfield. A future field-tier version needs a new estimator or asymptotic scope, such as varying clipping or unknown boundary geometry.
tldr: Under a scalar quadratic propensity boundary with uniformly bounded--Lipschitz nuisance functions, the fixed floor \(t n^{-2/3}\) leaves the nearest rare treated observations in the first-order law of the full-ATE cross-fitted clipped AIPW estimator. The project proves foldwise uniform transfer from total ratio histograms to an oracle score, identifies the resulting two-parameter compensated marked-Poisson law, and gives an explicit uniform law-level bridge: as \(t\downarrow0\) the fixed-law family approaches a centered \(3/2\)-stable law, whereas as \(t\to\infty\) deterministic and random-variance normalizations approach \(N(0,1)\). Entire-density and stable-quantile theory supports uniformly honest \(n^{-1/3}\)-length fitted-law intervals, with terminating numerical certification for rational interval names or converging certified parameter boxes.
gap: Published weak-overlap results separately cover oracle trimmed IPW non-Gaussian limits, untrimmed parametric doubly robust stable limits, and learned clipped AIPW Gaussian limits when the cutoff is larger than the critical floor. None supplies a feasible fixed-critical clipped-AIPW law and certified quantiles for the full ATE.
fill: A total cross-fitted estimator, uniform oracle transfer, explicit Lévy representation, parameter-uniform quantile certification, honest fitted-law intervals, and a joint random-variance characterization close this focused inference gap without a minimax claim.
